headline: THE RENA SHOWING IS CONFIRMED FOR 10:30 TOMORROW MORNING — booked at 1:57, confirmed at 3:41, access instructions sent at 3:42 — and the agent's very next message asked where the lake access is, which is a question you still owe an answer to tonight.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 REPEAT SHOWING — NOW CONFIRMED. Kyle B. of eXp Realty requested a SECOND tour at 1:57 PM for Friday 8/14 10:30–11:00 AM, and it was confirmed at 3:41. The ShowingTime notice proves it is his second: it prints "Showings by this Agent: 2". ⭐ THE PART THAT ARRIVED AFTER THE CONFIRMATION IS THE BUYING SIGNAL: Gene sent the access instructions at 3:42 and the agent came straight back at 3:47 asking where the lake access is. An agent who asks about amenities between booking and touring is pre-selling the house to somebody. ⚠️ THE CONTRADICTION IS STILL PRINTED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED — at 8:07 the same morning he texted, verbatim, "We have to get their house on the market befofe we look anymore." He booked five hours and fifty minutes later. Either those buyers reversed inside a morning, or he is bringing a different buyer. ⏰ It is the first repeat interest this listing has produced in 88 days, and it lands on the exact morning the listing agreement expires.
hotSignals.action: ⛔ ANSWER THE LAKE-ACCESS QUESTION TONIGHT — it was promised at 3:49 and it is the only thing this agent has actually asked you for. On the same call, ask the one question that matters: same buyers, or new ones. The answer arrives before the 10:30 tour, which is the last window where it can still change the price conversation you are having with the sellers the same day.

hotSignals.signal: 📞 A SECOND, SEPARATE BUYER SIGNAL ON THE SAME HOUSE THE SAME DAY — a buyer phoned directly at 9:33 AM asking for photos of the workshop and garage. Not an agent, not a form: a person who has studied the listing closely enough to know what is missing from it. ⚠️ IT SAT SEVEN AND A HALF HOURS. The voicemail arrives from a carrier address the sweep's standing query cannot see, so it was invisible to the automation until a hand-check at 5 PM found it — a real defect, now known and named rather than buried.
hotSignals.action: Call him back tonight and send the workshop and garage photos. Two independent buyer signals on day 88 of a listing that has produced one offer all summer is the strongest traffic day this file has had — and it lands the night before you rule the price.

It is the first read filed since the $4,000 cut went live 8/5, and the price objection that had appeared on every prior read is simply gone.

Call, don't email.

Seven reads on this listing, and every single price-recommendation field has come back blank.
hotSignals.action: No outreach — interested = No, so this falls outside the interested-feedback rule entirely. Use it as evidence in the two overdue agent calls: the objection on this house is layout, never price.

hotSignals.action: Call her — five days unworked. Ask what her buyer liked and whether size is a problem, because the other two reads that same Saturday both said the house is too small.

oweFeedback.when: 🔴 THREE ASKS AND TWENTY-THREE DAYS OF SILENCE — Tue 7/21, Wed 7/22 and Thu 7/23, from the RealtySouth Inverness listing side after your 7/21 1:00 PM tour. ⭐ THIS IS THE ONE THAT COSTS SOMETHING REAL, and the cost is not the courtesy — it is that the honest written answer IS your counter on the largest number on your board, roughly $36K of GCI. The listing side has asked repeatedly to be moved forward; a seller who reverse-offers a buyer is a seller who wants a deal. Twenty minutes of writing moves it. ⚠️ The appraisal figure your buyer cited as far under ask is single-sourced from him — do not quote it to the other side as an appraised value.
